verses.text: The word which came to Jeremiah from Yahweh in the days of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying,
“Go to the house of the Rechabites, and speak to them, and bring them into Yahweh’s house, into one of the rooms, and give them wine to drink.”
Then I took Jaazaniah the son of Jeremiah, the son of Habazziniah, and his brothers, and all his sons, and the whole house of the Rechabites;

and I brought them into Yahweh’s house, into the room of the sons of Hanan the son of Igdaliah, the man of God, which was by the room of the princes, which was above the room of Maaseiah the son of Shallum, the keeper of the threshold.
I set before the sons of the house of the Rechabites bowls full of wine, and cups; and I said to them, “Drink wine!”
But they said, “We will drink no wine; for Jonadab the son of Rechab, our father, commanded us, saying, ‘You shall drink no wine, neither you, nor your sons, forever.
You shall not build a house, sow seed, plant a vineyard, or have any; but all your days you shall dwell in tents; that you may live many days in the land in which you live.’
We have obeyed the voice of Jonadab the son of Rechab, our father, in all that he commanded us, to drink no wine all our days, we, our wives, our sons, or our daughters;
and not to build houses for ourselves to dwell in. We have no vineyard, field, or seed;
but we have lived in tents, and have obeyed, and done according to all that Jonadab our father commanded us.

But when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up into the land, we said, ‘Come, and let us go to Jerusalem for fear of the army of the Chaldeans, and for fear of the army of the Syrians; so we will dwell at Jerusalem.’”
Then Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah, saying,
“Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says: ‘Go, and tell the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, “Will you not receive instruction to listen to my words?” says Yahweh.

“The words of Jonadab the son of Rechab, that he commanded his sons, not to drink wine, are performed; and to this day they drink none, for they obey their father’s commandment: but I have spoken to you, rising up early and speaking; and you have not listened to me.

I have sent also to you all my servants the prophets, rising up early and sending them, saying, ‘Return now every man from his evil way, and amend your doings, and don’t go after other gods to serve them, and you will dwell in the land which I have given to you and to your fathers:’ but you have not inclined your ear, nor listened to me.
The sons of Jonadab the son of Rechab have performed the commandment of their father which he commanded them, but this people has not listened to me.”’

“Therefore Yahweh, the God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: ‘Behold, I will bring on Judah and on all the inhabitants of Jerusalem all the evil that I have pronounced against them; because I have spoken to them, but they have not heard; and I have called to them, but they have not answered.’”

Jeremiah said to the house of the Rechabites, “Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says: ‘Because you have obeyed the commandment of Jonadab your father, and kept all his precepts, and done according to all that he commanded you;’
therefore Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says: ‘Jonadab the son of Rechab shall not lack a man to stand before me forever.’”

footnotes.content: Jeremiah receives a word in King Jehoiakim's days—a time when the royal house is stiffening against God. The Lord doesn't abandon His people even when their rulers turn away. He sends His prophet with a strange task ahead, because love always finds a way to teach.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The command is oddly specific: bring the Rechabites into God's house and offer them wine. At first it sounds like a test of their loyalty, but it's really a kind of mirror—their steadfast refusal will show Judah's own failure to obey.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jaazaniah leads his whole household—brothers, sons, and servants. There's a quiet dignity here: a people bound together not by walls or cities, but by covenant with their ancestor Jonadab. They've chosen kinship over comfort.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They're brought into the temple itself, into the room of Hanan, "the man of God"—a sacred place. The setting is deliberate: this isn't a tavern or a feast-hall, but Yahweh's own house. And still they refuse to break their vow.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeremiah sets before them wine in abundance—not a small test, but a real temptation. He's not mocking them; he's inviting them to show what they're made of. The prophet's own hand offers the challenge.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They answer without hesitation: "We will drink no wine." Four centuries earlier, Jonadab gave them this rule—not as punishment, but as a way to keep them wandering, dependent only on God's care. They've held it all this time.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jonadab's command was radical: no houses, no fields, no vineyards. Stay in tents. It's a life of radical detachment—no roots in the land, no wealth to possess them. Yet he promised: "You shall live many days." Faithfulness bears its own fruit.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "We have obeyed the voice of Jonadab." Notice: they obey their father's voice as if it were still alive in them. Across generations, the command remains fresh, binding, honored. This is what covenant looks like—not written in stone but written in the heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "We have no vineyard, field, or seed." They state it plainly, almost with relief. What others crave—land, harvest, security—they've laid aside. In losing these, they've kept something priceless: a clear conscience and unbroken trust.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "We have lived in tents, and have obeyed." No complaint, no negotiation. Tents are portable, exposed, humble—yet they've made them their home. True obedience isn't grim; it's a way of life that becomes second nature.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When Nebuchadnezzar's armies drew near, they sought refuge in Jerusalem. But even fleeing danger, they hold fast—"we will dwell at Jerusalem" without breaking their covenant. Fear bends many, but not these.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The lesson pivots now: "Then Yahweh's word came to Jeremiah." The Rechabites have made their point through silence and steadfastness. Now Jeremiah speaks—the prophet will make the comparison explicit that the people's lives have made obvious.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Will you not receive instruction to listen to my words?" God's question is tender underneath its sharpness. He doesn't condemn them outright; He asks if they're willing to learn. Even now, the door of repentance stands open.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "The words of Jonadab are performed; but I have spoken to you, rising up early and speaking; and you have not listened to me." God compares Himself to Jonadab—both have given commands, both expect obedience. The Rechabites obey a man dead for centuries; Judah ignores the living God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "I have sent also to you all my servants the prophets, rising up early and sending them." The Lord's persistence is almost heartbreaking—He rises early and sends servants again and again. Every refusal breaks His heart, yet He keeps knocking.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "The sons of Jonadab have performed the commandment... but this people has not listened to me." The contrast is final now. One household keeps faith; a whole kingdom breaks it. Yet the Rechabites' faithfulness will become a mercy to others who witness and wonder.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "I will bring on Judah all the evil that I have pronounced against them." The judgment isn't capricious—it follows broken covenant and ignored prophets. Mercy rejected becomes accountability; grace spurned brings consequence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now Jeremiah turns to the Rechabites with blessing: "Because you have obeyed the commandment of Jonadab your father." They stand justified, not by their own righteousness, but by their faithfulness to a covenant they received.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Jonadab shall not lack a man to stand before me forever." His line will endure—a household that kept covenant through centuries of upheaval and exile. Readers today hear an echo: faithfulness isn't lost. Those who cleave to God's voice find themselves part of a lineage that never dies.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
